routes.label: Pair the angles and restrict the difference

question: Mary divides a circle into \(12\) sectors. The central angles of these sectors, measured in degrees, are all integers and they form an arithmetic sequence. What is the degree measure of the smallest possible sector angle?
solution:
Read the arithmetic sequence in nondecreasing order, reversing it if necessary. Let \(a\) be its smallest angle in degrees and \(d\) its common difference. Since sector angles are positive integers, \(a\ge1\) and \(d\ge0\) are integers. The angles are
\[
a,\ a+d,\ \ldots,\ a+11d.
\]
Pair the first angle with the last, the second with the next-to-last, and so on. Each of the six pairs has sum \(2a+11d\). Since the sectors fill a circle,
\[
6(2a+11d)=360,
\qquad 2a+11d=60.
\]
Both \(2a\) and \(60\) are even, so \(11d\), and hence \(d\), must be even. Also, \(a\ge1\) gives \(11d\le58\), so the integer \(d\) is at most \(5\). Thus all possibilities are \(d=0,2,4\), giving \(a=30,19,8\), respectively.

The smallest value, \(a=8\), is attainable: the twelve angles \(8,12,16,\ldots,52\) are positive integers and sum to \(6(8+52)=360\). Therefore the smallest possible sector angle is \(\boxed{8^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
